publisher: TheMoroccoAI.com (independent; not affiliated with the Government of Morocco)

classifications.VERIFIED FACT: An event, act or status that the cited source documents directly (for example, a signature, a launch or an appointment).
classifications.OFFICIAL TARGET: A quantified goal set by an official body. It is not an outcome and must not be read as achieved.
classifications.ANNOUNCED PLAN: A programme, institution or product an official body has announced or presented, whose operational delivery the registry has not verified.
classifications.INDEPENDENT ANALYSIS: An inference drawn by TheMoroccoAI from two or more records. It is labelled as interpretation, not as fact.
classifications.UNVERIFIED CLAIM: A statement attributed to a source whose underlying data the registry has not independently checked.

verification_statuses.verified: The source page was retrieved on the retrieval date and the excerpt was matched against it.
verification_statuses.partial: The source was retrieved but does not by itself carry every detail of the claim; the limitation is stated in verification_note.

records.title: Official launch of the national strategy "Maroc Digital 2030"
records.source_organization: MAP (Maghreb Arabe Presse), MAP Express
records.claim: The national strategy Digital Morocco 2030 (Maroc Digital 2030) was officially launched in Rabat on 25 September 2024 by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform.
source_excerpts: La Stratégie nationale "Maroc Digital 2030" (Digital Morocco 2030) a été officiellement lancée, mercredi à Rabat
Cette stratégie, lancée par le ministère de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l'administration
records.verification_note: The dispatch is dated 25 September 2024 (a Wednesday), matching "mercredi".

records.title: Digital Morocco 2030: stated job and e-government objectives
records.source_organization: MAP (Maghreb Arabe Presse), MAP Express
records.claim: Digital Morocco 2030 sets the objectives of 240,000 direct jobs with a contribution to GDP in 2030, digitalising public services, and moving Morocco from 113th to 50th place worldwide in the e-government development index.
source_excerpts: la création de 240.000 emplois directs et la contribution au produit intérieur brut (PIB) en 2030
digitaliser les services publics. Le but étant de faire passer le Maroc de la 113e à la 50e place mondiale dans l'indice de développement du e-gouvernement
records.verification_note: The source does not give a separate target year for the e-government ranking objective; 2030 is the strategy horizon. The starting point of 113th is the source's figure: no edition of the United Nations index ranks Morocco 113th, and it ranked 101st in 2022 and 90th in 2024 (MAI-EV-0046).

records.title: Head of Government statement on public digital investment, 2021–2024
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: The Head of Government stated that public investment dedicated to digital technology rose from MAD 11 million in 2021 to more than MAD 1.7 billion in 2024.
source_excerpts: public investment dedicated to digital technology has recorded unprecedented growth, rising from MAD 11 million in 2021 to more than MAD 1.7 billion in 2024
records.verification_note: The statement itself is verified on the government portal. The underlying budget figures were not checked against finance-law documents, so the figures are recorded as an attributed claim.

records.title: Inaugural National AI Conference opens in Rabat

The conference is structured around 13 thematic areas

records.title: Synthesis report of the First National AI Conference: Al Jazari Institute memorandum (Nador)
records.source_organization: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform

records.title: Synthesis report: agreement on sovereign green data-centre infrastructure

records.title: Synthesis report: UM6P data-centre partnership convention

records.title: Signature of the constitutive convention of the public-interest group "Institut Jazari ROOT"

source_excerpts: Casablanca, le 12 janvier 2026 - La Confédération Générale des Entreprises du Maroc (CGEM) a pris part à la cérémonie officielle de lancement du programme “AI Made in Morocco – L’IA au cœur de la transformation numérique et des services publics”, organisée par le Ministère de la Transition Numérique et de la Réforme de l’Administration.
a procédé à la signature de la convention constitutive du Groupement d’Intérêt Public (GIP) “Institut Jazari ROOT”, aux côtés de plusieurs départements ministériels et d’institutions publiques

records.title: Convention signed in Fès creating the Al-Jazari Institute for Industry "JAZARI Industrie X.0"

source_excerpts: Une convention a été signée, mardi 10 Mars à Fès, pour la création de l’Institut Al-Jazari pour l’Industrie "JAZARI Industrie X.0"

La convention a été signée par le ministère de l’Industrie et du Commerce, le ministère délégué chargé de la Transition numérique et de la Réforme de l’administration et le ministère de l’Economie et des Finances, d’une part, et les quatre université que compte la région Fès-Meknès. le développement de solutions innovantes reposant sur l’intelligence artificielle, l’Internet des objets, la robotique avancée et l’analyse des données industrielles

records.title: JAZARI network announced across the twelve regions; JAZARI ROOT as its core
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: In January 2026 the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform announced a network of "Jazari" institutes of excellence anchored in the twelve regions of the Kingdom, with JAZARI ROOT as its technical and strategic core, organised around e-government, smart rural and mountain zones, and major sporting events.
source_excerpts: l’ annonce, en janvier dernier, par le ministère de la transition numérique et de la réforme de l’administration de la mise en place du réseau des instituts "Jazari", une plateforme d’instituts d’excellence ancrés dans les douze régions du Royaume

Le noyau technique et stratégique de ce réseau repose sur l’institut "JAZARI ROOT" autour de trois thématiques clés, à savoir l’E-GOV, les smart zones rurales et montagneuses, ainsi que les grands événements sportifs.

records.title: Morocco AI 2030 roadmap: 2030 targets
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: The Morocco AI 2030 roadmap, presented by the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform, sets 2030 targets of MAD 100 billion in added value to GDP, 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, and 200,000 trained and certified AI talents.
source_excerpts: Morocco’s Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform on Tuesday in Rabat presented the main advances under the "Morocco AI 2030" roadmap

The roadmap, also referred to as “AI Made in Morocco,” aims by 2030 to generate 100 billion dirhams ($10 billion) in added value for the country’s GDP, create 50,000 direct and indirect jobs, and train and certify 200,000 AI talents
records.verification_note: These are targets. The source gives no progress figures towards them.

records.title: Morocco AI 2030 roadmap: pillars and the JAZARI Institutes network
records.source_organization: Maroc.ma (national portal of the Kingdom of Morocco)
records.claim: The Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform presented the Morocco AI 2030 roadmap in Rabat in September 2026. As presented, it is structured around three pillars (sovereignty and trust; innovation and competitiveness; impact, adoption and outreach) and relies on the national JAZARI Institutes network, described as comprising JAZARI ROOT, JAZARI Smart City, JAZARI EduTech and JAZARI Industrie X.0.
source_excerpts: Morocco’s Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform on Tuesday in Rabat presented the main advances under the "Morocco AI 2030" roadmap
The strategy is built around three pillars: sovereignty and trust, innovation and competitiveness, and impact, adoption and outreach.

Its implementation notably relies on the national network of JAZARI Institutes, the operational arm for AI research and innovation, comprising JAZARI ROOT, JAZARI Smart City, JAZARI EduTech and JAZARI Industrie X.0.
records.verification_note: The fact recorded is how the ministry described the roadmap's structure. The registry records no founding convention, nor any signing of one, for JAZARI Smart City or JAZARI EduTech.

records.title: Sovereign AI marketplace and the Idarati AI assistant presented

records.title: Atlas-Chat: Adapting Large Language Models for Low-Resource Moroccan Arabic Dialect (arXiv:2409.17912)
records.source_organization: arXiv (Shang et al.)
records.claim: A preprint first submitted on 26 September 2024 introduces Atlas-Chat, large language models for Moroccan Arabic (Darija) in 2B, 9B and 27B sizes, fine-tuned on an instruction dataset built by consolidating existing Darija resources, creating new manual and synthetic data, and translating English instructions.
source_excerpts: Atlas-Chat: Adapting Large Language Models for Low-Resource Moroccan Arabic Dialect

Focusing on Moroccan Arabic, also known as Darija, we construct our instruction dataset by consolidating existing Darija language resources, creating novel datasets both manually and synthetically, and translating English instructions with stringent quality control.
Atlas-Chat-2B, 9B, and 27B models, fine-tuned on the dataset
records.verification_note: A preprint, not peer-reviewed in this record. The abstract's priority claim ("first-ever") and benchmark comparisons are the authors' own and are not recorded as facts.

records.title: Atlas-Chat-9B model card

source_excerpts: Atlas-Chat is a family of open models instruction-tuned for Darija, the colloquial Arabic of Morocco
The model is developed by MBZUAI France Lab, an AI research center in Paris affiliated with the Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence (MBZUAI) headquartered in Abu Dhabi.
License: gemma
Base model google/gemma-2-9b Finetuned google/gemma-2-9b-it
records.verification_note: The publication date is the repository creation date reported by the Hugging Face API. The card's benchmark tables are self-reported and not recorded.

records.title: Darija-SFT-Mixture dataset card

records.claim: Darija-SFT-Mixture is published on Hugging Face as an instruction dataset of 458K samples in Darija, released under the ODC-BY licence with the note that some subsets carry non-commercial terms.
source_excerpts: Darija-SFT-Mixture is a dataset consisting of 458K instruction samples
Note the ODC-BY license , indicating that different licenses apply to subsets of the data. This means that some portions of the dataset are non-commercial.
records.verification_note: The publication date is the repository creation date reported by the Hugging Face API. The Atlas-Chat model cards list this dataset as their training data (MAI-EV-0022).

records.title: DarijaBERT model card
records.source_organization: Hugging Face (SI2M-Lab organisation)
records.claim: DarijaBERT is published on Hugging Face as a joint release of AIOX Lab and the SI2M Lab of INSEA: a model for written Moroccan Darija based on the BERT-base architecture without next-sentence-prediction pre-training, trained on about 3 million Darija sequences (691MB of text, about 100M tokens).
source_excerpts: AIOX Lab and SI2M Lab INSEA have joined forces
It is based on the same architecture as BERT-base, but without the Next Sentence Prediction (NSP) objective.
This model was trained on a total of ~3 Million sequences of Darija dialect representing 691MB of text or a total of ~100M tokens.
records.verification_note: Publication date left blank: the Hugging Face API reports 2022-03-02, the placeholder it assigns to repositories created before that date. The card's priority claim ("first BERT model") is not recorded. The card cites a 2023 paper by Gaanoun et al. that was not retrieved.

records.title: Al-Atlas-0.5B model card
records.source_organization: Hugging Face (atlasia organisation)

source_excerpts: Al-Atlas is a 0.5B parameter language model specifically trained on Moroccan Darija

Base model Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B

DEEPECHO - AX2021

records.title: UM6P Ventures case study: DeepEcho

source_excerpts: DeepEcho emerged from the startup studio "AIOX Labs"
DeepEcho, a Moroccan based startup
DeepEcho uses Machine Learning to improve outcomes for preventive and predictive diagnosis detection of prenatal complications.

The startup is also in the process of a FDA approval submission
records.verification_note: Investor's own publication; the PDF metadata gives a creation date of 8 May 2023. It is independent of DeepEcho but not of the investment it describes. Its accuracy figure and its statement about agreements with health centres are not recorded, as they were not independently checked. Company registration and headquarters address are not documented. Its 2023 statement about an FDA submission is consistent with, but does not by itself identify, the applicant of FDA 510(k) K242594 (MAI-EV-0032).

records.title: DeepEcho website: product description and regulatory disclaimer
records.source_organization: DeepEcho
records.claim: DeepEcho describes its software as using AI and deep learning to help radiologists and minimally trained clinicians with ultrasound video diagnosis, and states on its website that its claims and metrics are not yet validated by the FDA and come from its own clinical studies under scientific and regulatory review.
source_excerpts: Deepecho uses Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning to mimic what a trained sonographer would do and help radiologists and minimally trained clinicians with ultrasound video diagnosis.
Claims, figures, metrics & any kind of scientific and / or marketing materials listed in the current website are not validated yet by the FDA.
Metrics comes from our own clinical studies (currently under scientific & regulatory review)
records.verification_note: The disclaimer is quoted as the site showed it on the retrieval date, but it appears outdated: the FDA database lists 510(k) clearance K242594 for a DEEPECHO device on 23 May 2025 (MAI-EV-0032, MAI-EV-0039), and the Moroccan government says DeepEcho's solution obtained FDA "approbation" (MAI-EV-0033). It is therefore no longer used to establish a lifecycle stage: a quotation that still matches its source can support a claim that is no longer current. Accuracy and speed figures on the site are self-reported and not recorded.

officialiser la prise de fonction de Azeddine Zroura en tant que nouveau Directeur Général de la filiale marocaine

records.verification_note: A 510(k) "substantially equivalent" decision is a US market clearance, which the FDA distinguishes from premarket approval (PMA). The record names no Moroccan entity: its association with the Morocco-based DeepEcho rests on the matching name and device type, the deepecho.io e-mail domain and Moroccan data sites in the 510(k) summary (MAI-EV-0039), UM6P Ventures' 2023 statement that the startup was preparing an FDA submission (MAI-EV-0028) and the Moroccan government's statement (MAI-EV-0033). records.verification_note: The verified fact is the signature and the stated framework. records.verification_note: Primary regulatory document. A 510(k) clearance permits marketing in the United States; the FDA distinguishes it from premarket approval (PMA). records.title: TOUBKAL: peer-reviewed description of the system and its reported workloads
records.source_organization: The Journal of Supercomputing (Springer)
records.claim: A peer-reviewed article in The Journal of Supercomputing, by authors affiliated with Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing, describes Toubkal's GPU partitions (NVIDIA A100 nodes from the initial 2022 deployment and H100 nodes added in 2025). It states that fine-tuning of transformer-based large language models and large-scale computational fluid dynamics simulations have been run on the system, and presents as a benchmark the fine-tuning runs that produced the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija language models, which it attributes to "Belkasmi et al." while citing the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj et al.
source_excerpts: TOUBKAL: a high-performance supercomputer powering scientific research in Africa
The initial deployment in 2022 included five Dell XE8545 nodes with dual AMD EPYC 7713 CPUs and four NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs per node.
In 2025, three Dell XE8640 nodes were added, each with dual Intel Xeon Platinum 8468 CPUs and four NVIDIA H100-HBM3-80GB GPUs.

we examine practical workloads such as fine-tuning transformer-based large language models (LLMs) and conducting large-scale computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, both of which have been successfully run on Toubkal.
we present a practical benchmark demonstrating the fine-tuning of a large language model (LLM) performed on the Toubkal supercomputer by Belkasmi et al.
This work led to the creation of GemMaroc
records.verification_note: Open-access article (CC BY 4.0), published online 3 October 2025. Every author lists an affiliation with the university that hosts and runs Toubkal, so the workload statement is the operator's own report, peer-reviewed but not independent. It documents specific fine-tuning runs, not the scale, share or continuity of AI use. The article names their authors "Belkasmi et al.", but its reference [57] is the GemMaroc preprint by Skiredj, Azhari, Atou, Tazi and Berrada (MAI-EV-0042); that preprint does not itself say where the runs were made. The article's statement that they ran on Toubkal comes from its own authors, none of whom is an author of the preprint. The article's user counts and utilisation figures are not recorded. Benchmark, accuracy and energy figures in the article are not recorded. The verified fact is what the article states. Excerpts were matched against the article page retrieved on the retrieval date; automated requests to the publisher can receive a bot-challenge page, which the source checker reports as blocked and does not bypass.

records.title: GemMaroc: the preprint describing the GemMaroc fine-tuning runs
records.source_organization: arXiv (preprint by Skiredj, Azhari, Atou, Tazi and Berrada)
records.claim: The preprint introducing the GemMaroc Moroccan Darija language models, by three authors from Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing, one from Hugging Face and one from the National Institute of Posts and Telecoms, reports that its fine-tuning experiments ran on two NVIDIA A100-80GB GPUs, and the 27-billion-parameter GemMaroc model on eight NVIDIA H100-80GB GPUs, taking about 48 GPU-hours. It expresses the total cost as a cloud cost, using a public on-demand rate in a Runpod Cloud region, and does not name the computing facility used.
source_excerpts: College of Computing, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, Benguerir, Morocco
All fine-tuning experiments were conducted on 2×A100-80GB GPUs, except for our largest model, the 27-billion-parameter GEMMAROC, which was fine-tuned on 8×H100-80GB GPUs.
consuming approximately 48 GPU-hours and keeping the total cloud cost well under $100.
Based on the public on-demand rate of $2 per A100-hour in the selected Runpod Cloud region.
records.verification_note: arXiv preprint, version 1 of 20 May 2025, not peer-reviewed; excerpts matched against the PDF. The excerpt on the hardware was checked against the rendered page: the PDF's text layer splits the small-capital model name and drops the hyphen in "H100-80GB" at a line break, so automated matching reports it missing. No author is named Belkasmi: the Toubkal article (MAI-EV-0041) attributes these runs to "Belkasmi et al." but its reference [57] is this preprint by Skiredj et al. The preprint does not mention Toubkal, the African Supercomputing Centre or any acknowledgement of computing resources; its cost footnote uses a commercial cloud provider's public rate, which may be a costing convention rather than where the runs took place. It therefore neither confirms nor rules out that the runs were made on Toubkal. Three of the five authors are affiliated with the university that runs Toubkal.

records.title: GeneLM: genomic language model trained on the Toubkal supercomputer
records.source_organization: Briefings in Bioinformatics (Oxford University Press); Akotenou and El Allali
records.claim: A peer-reviewed article by two researchers of Mohammed VI Polytechnic University's College of Computing reports that the coding-sequence classification experiments for their bacterial genomic language model were conducted on the Toubkal supercomputer, with training on two NVIDIA A100 80GB GPUs for a total of 37 hours over two epochs.
source_excerpts: The CDS classification experiments were conducted on the Toubkal supercomputer.
The training was performed on two NVIDIA A100 GPUs, each equipped with 80GB of memory.
the total training duration was 37 h for two epochs.
providing access to the supercomputing resources (cc.um6p.ma/toubkal-super-computer)
records.verification_note: Open-access article (CC BY), published 3 July 2025. The publisher's site refuses automated requests, so the excerpts were matched against the full text deposited in Europe PMC (PMC12222049). Both authors are affiliated with the university that runs Toubkal: this is the researchers' own account of one training run, not independent documentation, and it says nothing of Toubkal's overall AI use, its scale or its continuity.

records.title: Ministry release: memorandum signed on the Nexus AI Factory platform
records.source_organization: Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform (mmsp.gov.ma)
records.claim: The ministry's own news release states that, on the sidelines of GITEX Africa Morocco 2026, Nexus Core Systems, the Ministry of Digital Transition and Administration Reform, the Ministry of Investment, Convergence and Evaluation of Public Policies, and the Moroccan Agency for Investment and Export Development (AMDIE) signed a memorandum of understanding on the "Nexus AI Factory Plateform" project, described as combining a high-performance computing data centre, a centre of excellence and an innovation hub.

Le projet repose sur une montée en puissance technologique soutenue par un investissement initial de 12 milliards de dirhams mobilisé sur deux phases qui visent la création de 125 emplois directs fin 2027
Phase 1 – Hub de Nouaceur : Une enveloppe de 5 milliards de dirhams sera consacrée à l'activation d'une capacité de 16 MW sur le site de Nouaceur.
Ce déploiement portera la capacité cumulée à 36 MW fin 2027.
records.verification_note: Release by a signatory, dated 8 April 2026; the verified fact is the signature of the memorandum. Despite the words "lancement opérationnel", the phase investment, capacity and job figures are stated in the future tense, as commitments. The release describes the MAD 12 billion as an "investissement initial" "mobilisé sur deux phases"; that wording does not establish that any amount has been spent, and the release documents no expenditure. Nothing in the release shows construction or operation. Spellings are as printed ("Plateform", "Exporattions"). The other two signatories (the investment ministry and AMDIE) are not entities in this registry. The release does not reproduce the memorandum, and this registry has not obtained its text.

records.verification_note: Official gazette, Arabic general edition, pages 5224 to 5229; the French translation edition had not been published on the retrieval date (French editions up to 7544 were checked). Excerpts were transcribed from the page images, because the PDF's text layer reverses Arabic word order; automated excerpt matching cannot be relied on for this record. The orders approve conventions that are annexed to the original orders; the gazette does not reproduce them and, as article 2 of each order provides, publishes only a summary of each. This registry has not obtained the signed texts. The record is a legal establishment act, not the signed text, and it gives no signing dates. Each group is created for thirty years with a statutory seat (JAZARI Industrie X.0 at the Euro-Mediterranean University of Fès). The summaries name further founding members (for JAZARI ROOT, the Secretary-General of the Government, several ministries, national police, the CNDP, the Digital Development Agency and the Rabat-Salé-Kénitra regional council; for JAZARI EduTech and JAZARI Smart City, further ministries and public bodies; the Industrie X.0 summary names no members beyond the seven recorded here) that are not recorded as relationships here. No act concerns the Al Jazari institute in Nador.
